Indyke worked at Gold and Wachtel from 1986 to 1988 as a pre-law clerk, where he first encountered Epstein as a firm client, then attended Cornell Law School, graduating in 1991 [Finding #2100]. A November 2003 FedEx invoice from NYSG LLC at 457 Madison Avenue documents Darren shipping a package to Bernard, placing him at Epstein's 457 Madison office by that date [Finding #2104, EFTA01318608].

Indyke returned to Gold and Wachtel as a corporate and intellectual property associate from 1991 to 1995, spent 1995-1996 at Greenberg Traurig, then left conventional legal practice to work for Jeffrey Epstein circa 1996 [Finding #2100]. His earliest FEC filing (2000) lists his employer as "J Epstein and Co Inc" at a New York City 10002 address; by 2003 this had shifted to "New York Strategy Group LLC" at 301 East 66th Street — a building associated with Epstein entity 301 East 66th Street Associates LP, where Indyke himself resided in Apartment 8D [Finding #1725, Finding #448]. A Deutsche Bank KYC memo summarized his source of wealth as "in-house lawyer for Epstein at Southern Financial LLC for over 15 years" [Finding #310, EFTA01297200]. His own early business entity, DKI Graphics Inc (NY Corp #1695791, filed January 1993), went inactive, along with a DBA for New York Strategy Group LLC filed in January 2000 at 457 Madison Avenue, by which point his practice was effectively Epstein-centric [Finding #2142, EFTA01296686, Finding #1746].

sections.title: Corporate Architecture
sections.content:
Indyke's Deutsche Bank KYC file lists 50 employment records and 23 business associations, spanning officer positions at Nine East 71st Street Corporation (from 1989), 116 East 65th Street LLC (from 2000), 6975 Morse Road LLC (from 2001), Max Hotel Services Corp (CEO), E Management New York LLC (agent and process server), Zorro Development Corp (Secretary, in New Mexico), and others [Finding #1761, EFTA01295770]. He served as Secretary at Southern Trust Company and Authorized Signatory at Southern Financial LLC, the two Epstein corporate vehicles that sat above much of the wider entity web [Finding #311, EFTA02635112]. Darren K. Indyke PLLC itself was incorporated as a NY Domestic Professional Service LLC on September 5, 2008 at 575 Lexington Avenue 4th Floor [Finding #1711, EFTA01297934].

A cross-reference of state and international registry filings indicates the architecture extended across at least five jurisdictions [Finding #1541]. In the USVI, Indyke was VP and Secretary of Poplar Inc., Trustee of the Haze Trust (from 1999), and Treasurer then Vice President of Gratitude America Ltd (2012-2019) [Finding #1717]. In Florida, SunBiz filings list him as sole manager of 124 Parc Monceau LLC (a Paris-property entity formed August 22, 2013 and voluntarily dissolved January 25, 2017) and manager of Harlequin Dane LLC, his personal entity from 2015 [Finding #516, Finding #1541]. In New Mexico, Secretary of State filings name him as Secretary of Zorro Development Corp [Finding #1541]. Registry records also show a co-ownership interest in Paris-SCIJEP, an LLC in France [Finding #1541]. The Florida Science Foundation (FL SunBiz N07000010684), where Indyke served as Assistant Director at 457 Madison Avenue, operated from November 2007 to its administrative dissolution in September 2009 — a period that spans Epstein's Florida plea deal and the work-release arrangement that allowed him 16-hour daily departures from jail [Finding #510, Finding #1708].

An email exchange from March 2019 illustrates how Indyke handled ownership questions at Epstein's direction. When forming Truth Robot LLC, Indyke asked Epstein whether to name SF LLC or STC as the manager. Epstein responded: "Cant have my name." Indyke replied: "Will delete and have Rich sign as Treasurer of Southern Financial LLC" [Finding #1738, EFTA02637769, EFTA02635112]. On its face, the exchange documents Indyke structuring the operating agreement to remove Epstein's name from the filing and substitute Richard Kahn signing in a corporate capacity.

sections.title: Financial Flows and Cash Structuring
sections.content:
Deutsche Bank records show DKIP PLLC (account #42953707) functioning as a three-purpose vehicle: law firm payroll, a conduit for Epstein-entity transactions, and a destination for post-death estate liquidation [Finding #2208]. Epstein funded the firm's operations through $250,000 monthly transfers from his JPMorgan DDA account [#739110438], which covered ADP payroll disbursements of $45,000 to $50,000 per month [Finding #2191, EFTA01503821]. The Deutsche Bank balance peaked at roughly $600,000 in November 2014; across the tracked history the account processed approximately $5.95 million outgoing and $5.57 million incoming, about $11.5 million in gross flows [Finding #2208]. A Deutsche Bank KYC note recorded a $414,000 DKIP PLLC balance as of 2015 [Finding #310, EFTA01297200].

One of the largest documented transactions was a $350,000 wire from DKIP PLLC to FirstBank Puerto Rico for the account of FT Real Estate Inc., an Epstein USVI C-corporation, on November 6, 2014 [Finding #1721, EFTA01285197]. The same day, Indyke's account received a $600,000 deposit from Epstein, consistent with the law firm serving as a pass-through for a Caribbean real estate transaction [Finding #2193]. A separate wire of $25,000 to an unknown recipient on September 12, 2014 was the earliest DS10 wire from the account, funded by a fresh deposit into what had been a $0 balance [Finding #2203, Finding #1721, EFTA01285114].

On June 17, 2016, a single day's wire report shows roughly $1.27 million in Indyke-connected disbursements from Epstein's Deutsche Bank account: $1 million and $50,000 to Harlequin Dane LLC (Indyke's personal entity), $220,000 to Cory Carlesimo/Carrie Shumway via Merrill Lynch at 570 Lexington Avenue (adjacent to the DKIP office), and $108,000 to Endicott Opportunity Partners IV LP [Finding #2195, Finding #2212, EFTA01299462]. The $1 million payment was structured as a 9-year loan from Southern Financial LLC at the IRS Applicable Federal Rate of 1.41%, as reflected in Richard Kahn's email requesting approval: "please confirm ok to transfer 1,000,000 to Harlequin Dane LLC (darren entity) for 9 year loan from SFL LLC" [Finding #2195, EFTA02460458]. The only documented repayment on that $1 million-plus loan was a $51,000 transfer from Harlequin Dane to Southern Financial on May 2, 2019, two months before Epstein's arrest, which Southern Financial moved out to Citibank the next day [Finding #2196, EFTA01377570, EFTA01389013].

Deutsche Bank AML flagged both the DKIP PLLC account and Epstein's personal account [#35269691] for cash structuring in July 2017, citing three instances since July 2016 of cashing checks just below the $10,000 Currency Transaction Report threshold [Finding #313, Finding #1731, EFTA01346023]. On April 26, 2017, Indyke brought two checks to Deutsche Bank's 345 Park Avenue branch — one drawn on Epstein's account under power of attorney and one on his own DKIP account — and on a prior occasion had "inquired on if a CTR will have to be done" when cashing a $7,500 check for Epstein [Finding #1731, EFTA01345992]. The pattern led to a SAR filing and an internal compliance meeting on July 25, 2017 attended by Stewart Oldfield and other Deutsche Bank personnel [Finding #1731, EFTA01346029]. Separately, Indyke picked up $40,000 in cash plus Euros from Epstein's personal accounts [Finding #313, EFTA01345568]. Indyke's DKIP PLLC also made $8,082 and $3,057 payments to BankUnited in May and July 2018 under a "M. YOM" notation; the amounts and recurrence are consistent with mortgage or loan payments on Indyke personal property funded through the Epstein-sourced account [Finding #2200, EFTA01287585, EFTA01287749].

In April 2019, Indyke coordinated receipt of a $250,000 wire transfer from Andy Faulkner via United Community Bank, split into two tranches ($240,000 + $10,000) to work around the bank's online wiring limit; the split was confirmed by Kahn at HBRK Associates [Finding #1692, Finding #1740, EFTA02634130].

sections.title: DKIP as Operational Control Center
sections.content:
Internal emails show DKIP PLLC operating as Epstein's day-to-day communications hub, with staff placing calls on his behalf to figures including Leon Black, Christina Devernois, Bill Scherer, and others [Finding #1704, EFTA02355134]. A December 17, 2010 email from the office reads: "Peggy is only one we did not call. I have called Leon Black, Christina Devernois (he has called you back), Bill Scherer, Michelle, Kevin Law..."; Epstein replied from his iPhone, "Did we finish calls?" [Finding #1704, EFTA02355134]. Legal assistant Bebe Avdiu (bebe.dkipllc@gmail.com) managed scheduling, medical appointments, travel arrangements, and congressional outreach, including contact with "Commissioner Henry's office" in February 2018 [Finding #348, EFTA02238828]. In February 2018, Avdiu also emailed Epstein's instruction to gather Elina Arsenyeva's address, date of birth, Social Security number, and photo ID through the law firm rather than an HR channel [Finding #1729, EFTA02242015]. Indyke operated from dual offices at 575 Lexington Avenue 4th Floor in New York and 5300 W. Atlantic Avenue Suite 602 in Delray Beach, Florida by early 2019, with FL addresses appearing on DKIP email traffic from February through April [Finding #1724, Finding #1750, EFTA02634130].

Indyke was looped into monitoring and information-control traffic. When a British journalist anchored a rental boat near Little St. James Island in March 2011, USVI staff reported the incident to both Epstein and Indyke (CC: DKIPKLC), noting the reporter "was there for about 3 hours" and "probably left because it is raining heavily" [Finding #1728, EFTA01837558]. In May 2019, when a caller named "Nova" phoned Southern Trust Company asking what Financial Trust did, Kahn identified him as a journalist and staff discussed changing the phone greeting from "Southern Trust" to simply "2525" — the street address — to obscure the entity name; Indyke was copied on the correspondence [Finding #1744, EFTA02288520].

Indyke also forwarded Google Alerts for "Jeffrey Epstein" and political news items to Epstein across 2014-2019 [Finding #1742, Finding #1753]. These included a 2016 email about a James Patterson book alleging a federal cover-up of Epstein's crimes, which led Indyke to coordinate a legal response with attorney Charles Michael and draft a letter to the publisher's counsel [Finding #1742, HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_031307]. He forwarded a Gloria Allred interview on Trump misconduct allegations and a "Rigging the Election" DNC video to Epstein in October-November 2016 [Finding #1753]. In August 2018, Deutsche Bank ran an adverse-media screen of Indyke; analyst Mayur Rathod concluded on September 3, 2018: "Confirmed, no adverse information in web results for Darren Indyke" [Finding #1720, Finding #1748, EFTA01297934, EFTA01298405].

sections.title: Wexner Connection
sections.content:
Indyke had a documented professional relationship with the Wexner family beyond his Epstein work. He served as Secretary of The Wexner Foundation (a Foreign Not-For-Profit Corp registered in New York, DOS #2405489) and appeared in Leslie Wexner's SC 13D/A SEC filing for TOO Inc. (later Bath & Body Works) in March 2001, the only EDGAR filing naming Indyke directly [Finding #1718, EDGAR:0000909518-01-000297]. This places Indyke in a Wexner SEC compliance role as early as 2001, during the period when the Epstein-Wexner relationship was still intact [Finding #1718].

A January 23, 2008 ACRIS record documents Abigail S. Wexner transferring a property interest at 15 Central Park West, Unit 10B (Block 1114, Lot 1507 Manhattan) to Darren K. Indyke [Finding #2105, ACRIS:2008012900966001]. The document type is PAT (deed/patent). Whether this was executed in a fiduciary or personal capacity is not established in the dossier record; the filing itself places a direct real-property transfer between Wexner's wife and Epstein's personal attorney into the public ACRIS index [Finding #2105]. The Limited Inc. and the broader Wexner corporate ecosystem made up a substantial portion of Indyke's non-Epstein work during the 1998-2001 period [Finding #1718].

sections.title: Pre-Arrest Activity (2019)
sections.content:
In the months before Epstein's July 6, 2019 arrest, DKIP output across legal, logistical, and operational tasks ran heavy. In March 2019, Indyke arranged Epstein's passport renewal through G3 Visas and Passports at the Miami Passport Agency, with the new passport issued March 8 — the same day Epstein emailed about a Russian visa transfer [Finding #1448, EFTA02278714]. He handled Karyna Shuliak's divorce affidavit, managed DPNR permit violation investigations at the USVI property with local attorney Chris Kroblin of Kellerhals Ferguson Kroblin reporting to him, and tracked Epstein's day-counts across jurisdictions to establish USVI tax residency: "The idea is that I am trying to establish that he travels frequently out of the USVI. I know he does, but maybe we might want to quantify" [Finding #315, Finding #1694, Finding #1707, Finding #1733, EFTA02283344, EFTA02631816]. He also coordinated a March 13 message about a woman named Daphne who was "still at the Island. No one showed up. How long should we keep her there?" — sent from a newly-created dki.birchtreebr@gmail.com address [Finding #1712, Finding #1767, EFTA02630972].

In early April 2019, Indyke compiled victim evidence excerpts for Epstein's defense, including police report pages and deposition transcripts. One page referencing Epstein "masturbating" drew particular attention; Indyke wrote to Epstein, "I am thinking that we keep it out," before Epstein approved sending the full package to "Jack" [Finding #1695, EFTA02634581]. A "First Draft of Talking Points" dated April 3 asserted that "Mr. Epstein has diligently and fully complied with all applicable registration obligations under federal and local law" [Finding #1698, Finding #1699, EFTA02632963]. On April 8, Indyke contacted Angel Watch, the SMART Office (three calls), and ICE's Child Exploitation Cybercrimes division to work through sex offender registration requirements, finding that Angel Watch had "no warm bodies" to speak with and was directed to an email inbox at dhsintermeganslaw@ice.dhs.gov [Finding #1691, EFTA02633922]. Indyke also drafted revised "Offer to Purchase PA Shares" documents on March 14, 2019 for partnership interests in an Epstein-linked entity [Finding #1697, EFTA02634086], and arranged meetings on March 20 between Epstein and defense lawyers Scott Link, Marty Weinberg, and Laura Menninger — Menninger also being Ghislaine Maxwell's defense attorney [Finding #1709, EFTA02239640].

Over the same weeks, Indyke was negotiating the purchase of a Sikorsky S-76 helicopter, drafting the Asset Purchase Agreement and coordinating pre-purchase inspections with pilot Larry Visoski; Indyke himself was scheduled for S-76 recurrent pilot training at FlightSafety Palm Beach in May 2019, confirming he held a helicopter pilot rating [Finding #1701, EFTA02636796]. On February 13, he alerted Epstein's inner circle — including Richard Kahn, Bella Klein, Jeanne Brennan, and Cecile de Jongh — that his dkiesq@aol.com account had suffered "unauthorized uses," shifting communications to dki.birchtreebr@gmail.com [Finding #1705, Finding #1696, EFTA02275663].

sections.title: Maxwell Property Arrangement
sections.content:
Deutsche Bank due diligence records list Indyke and Ghislaine Maxwell as "Other Associates" at the same physical address from November 2008 to September 2015 [Finding #1762, EFTA01295770]. The address was 116 East 65th Street, a property purchased by Indyke that, according to a Daily Mail report cited in the same Deutsche Bank file, was "promptly split into apartments, one of which is now Ms Maxwell's residence" [Finding #1762, EFTA01295770]. Per the same file, the arrangement placed Maxwell in a residence held by Epstein's attorney rather than by Maxwell or Epstein directly [Finding #1762].

Indyke's connections to Maxwell extended beyond real estate. Both donated $4,000 to Gary King for Congress (New Mexico) in 2004 — Indyke from New York, Maxwell from St. Thomas, V.I. — in the state where Epstein's Zorro Ranch was located [Finding #448]. Indyke also signed corporation paperwork for Sarah Kellen's design business in 2012 [Finding #1710]. Common Interest Agreement privilege logs from Epstein's legal defense show Indyke coordinating legal strategy with Maxwell's attorneys [Finding #1321].

sections.title: Post-Death and Estate Administration
sections.content:
Indyke and Richard Kahn were named co-executors of the Estate of Jeffrey E. Epstein, co-trustees of the 1953 Trust (created August 8, 2019, two days before Epstein's death), co-trustees of the Epstein 2019 Trust, and co-beneficiaries of the Butterfly Trust alongside Karyna Shuliak [Finding #312, EFTA01266204]. Indyke was designated a $50 million beneficiary in Epstein's will [Finding #1708]. The 1953 Trust was renamed or established 48 hours before Epstein died in MCC custody; that timing is a documented fact of the estate record, not an established intent [Finding #312].

Deutsche Bank account liquidation records from November 2019 show DKIP PLLC receiving $5,566,408.92 on November 20, with $4.66 million moving to an unknown recipient the same day [Finding #2197]. Two weeks later, Kahn's HBRK Associates received $9.24 million across seven transfers, and Kahn personally received $98,800; analysis of the liquidation records puts the combined post-death transfers to the co-executors at an estimated $14.9 million [Finding #2197]. Indyke oversaw the Epstein Victims Compensation Program, which paid more than $120 million to over 130 survivors, and managed the disposition of Epstein's major properties: the Manhattan townhouse at 9 East 71st Street, the Palm Beach estate, the New Mexico ranch, and the USVI islands. DKIP also arranged storage of 11 boxes under account #4361 at an unnamed storage facility, with box-number formats that indicate documents from multiple sources [Finding #1693, EFTA02237523].

Federal court filings name Indyke as a co-executor defendant in more than 30 lawsuits across SDNY, SDFL, and NDGA, with plaintiffs including Annie Farmer and multiple Doe plaintiffs; docket records list Troutman Pepper Hamilton Sanders LLP as his counsel in these proceedings, with Bennet Moskowitz as attorney of record [Finding #1723]. In a separate 2021 action, JEGE LLC — an Epstein aviation entity — and Thomas Huff filed a fraud lawsuit against Indyke and Kahn in N.D. Georgia, an Epstein-insider entity suing the estate executors [Finding #1726]. The USVI Attorney General's 2021 amended complaint included the most detailed allegations against Indyke personally, including management of 140-plus bank accounts and facilitation of payments to women with Eastern European surnames [Finding #1708]. The $105 million-plus settlement in 2022 resolved the USVI claims without admission of liability [Finding #1708].

sections.title: Congressional Scrutiny and Current Status
sections.content:
On August 25, 2025, the House Oversight Committee subpoenaed Indyke alongside Les Wexner and Richard Kahn, with testimony scheduled for March 5, 2026 [Finding #1703]. Survivors told the Committee that Indyke and Kahn "knew about Epstein's abuse and helped facilitate his crimes through management of legal and financial affairs" [Finding #1703]. Indyke's defense attorney Daniel Weiner has represented him in both the USVI civil litigation and the congressional proceedings [Finding #1715]. Criminal defense attorney Marc Agnifilo, who also represented NXIVM leader Keith Raniere, has separately served as Indyke's attorney [Finding #1715].

Indyke joined Parlatore Law Group LLP as Of Counsel in October 2022; the firm was founded by Timothy Parlatore, who previously represented Donald Trump in the classified documents investigation and represents Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth [Finding #1715]. Indyke departed in January 2026, coinciding with the DOJ's release of 3.5 million Epstein files [Finding #1715]. He operates as a licensed Florida real estate agent with Luxury Partners Realty in Delray Beach and runs The Indyke Law Firm PLLC (FL entity L22000043914, formed 2022) from 16065 Bristol Isle Way, Delray Beach [Finding #1706]. His Le Lac Road property in Boca Raton, purchased in 2015 for $3.1 million without a mortgage, sold in May 2023 for $5.5 million [Finding #1706].

Indyke appears in more than 130 documents in the November 2024 DOJ email release and is referenced in 96 documents on EpsteinExposed.com. The Cornell Daily Sun covered both Indyke (JD '91) and Reid Weingarten ('71) as Cornell Law alumni named in the Epstein files [Finding #1714].
